column6: F: Last time the server was dead for orders and invoices. Now the building model too? | M: Same idea, now for a model. Two people, one model, still no server in the middle.

column4: how card · what you are watching
column5: M: Proof of concept again. | F: And what is real? | M: The Modeller is.
column6: M: Same promise as before. This is a proof of concept, not a product. | F: So what is real here, and what is not? | M: The Modeller you see is the real one. The small Team chip at the bottom corner, and the pairing page, are a test bench. In daily work you would only see the chip.

column4: phone/laptop clip · pairing by code · TEST BENCH
column5: F: How do two browsers join? | M: A code you can read out loud.
column6: F: How do the two screens become a team? | M: The same way as before. One starts a space, the other joins with a short code, and the first one approves it. Fresh space, so nothing old is mixed in.

column4: laptop clip · draw a block · Visit · second screen Visit · block appears
column5: M: One draws a block. | F: And the other sees it? | M: After a visit, yes.
column6: M: On the first screen we draw a block and press Visit. That drops a sealed letter in the post box. | F: And the second screen? | M: It had nothing on it. It presses Visit, picks up the letter, and the same block appears, in the same place. We check the position by numbers, not by eye.

column4: laptop clip · move the block · Visit on both · same spot
column5: F: What if it moves? | M: A move is its own letter.
column6: F: And if somebody moves the block? | M: A move is a small letter of its own. Left, right, or backwards, it arrives exactly. After the visit both screens agree on where the block is, to a millionth of a metre.

column4: both screens · each moves a different block · Visit · both moves present
column5: F: Two people, two blocks? | M: Both moves count.
column6: F: What if we each move a different block at the same time? | M: Then nobody is in the way. Both moves arrive, and both screens end up with both blocks moved. Same rule as the orders: different things never clash.

column4: both screens · same block, same direction · warning on both · block stays
column5: F: And the same block? | M: Then nobody silently wins.
column6: F: And if we both push the same block in the same direction? | M: Then nobody silently wins. Both screens show the warning, with both values, and the block stays where you both last agreed. Only the direction you both touched is held. A move you made in another direction still goes through.

column4: laptop clip · one more move after seeing both · warning clears
column5: F: How does it end? | M: Someone decides, by moving it again.
column6: F: How does the warning go away? | M: Someone who has seen both moves just moves it again. That counts as the decision. The warning clears on both screens and the block sits in one place. A proper chooser button is still to be built.

column4: limits card · what is shared today · what stays on your own device
column5: F: Is everything shared? | M: No. Drawing and moving only.
column6: F: Is every tool shared now? | M: Honestly, no. Drawing a block and moving it are shared. Cuts, rotations and most other tools stay on your own device for now, and the corner chip says so. Also not done yet: who may touch which floor or trade. That needs a small addition to the post office rules.

column5: F: So, a model without a server? | M: A proof of concept that passed its tests.
column6: F: So, a shared model with no server? | M: A proof of concept, and every claim in it is a test that passed. The ERP and the Modeller use the same post office. Thanks for watching!
